bullets.title: META +6.6% on Muse AI agent launch; key outperformer in down market
bullets.body: META surged 6.6% on the release of Muse, a consumer AI agent for task automation (emails, scheduling, shopping), standing out as the primary outperformer on a day when S&P 500 fell 0.48% and NDX fell 0.3%. Tech sector was broadly weak with software -0.5% and internet -1.1%.

bullets.title: AAPL: Foldable iPhone Duo debuts at $1,999; iPhone 18 Pro up $100 y/y to $1,199
bullets.body: Apple unveiled the foldable iPhone Duo (5.4" outer / 7.6" unfolded, titanium, A20 Pro 2nm chip, preorder Oct 16, ships Oct 23 at $1,999) alongside iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max at $1,199/$1,299, up $100 y/y. UBS and carriers (AT&T/T-Mobile offering up to $1,199 trade-in credits) expect ~20 bps y/y industry upgrade rate decline in 3Q-4Q as higher pricing weighs on demand. AAPL shares were -0.3% on the day.

bullets.title: CMCSA -6.6%: CFO flags Q3 broadband subscriber losses won't improve y/y
bullets.body: Comcast CFO at Goldman Sachs conference stated Q3 broadband net subscriber losses will not improve year-over-year, driving shares down 6.6%. Goldman data shows 3Q net adds ~-87k vs -91k y/y — still worsening y/y despite sequential improvement. Orlando theme parks also softening in 3Q.

bullets.title: NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MRVL, ARM: Piper Sandler initiates all Overweight
bullets.body: Piper Sandler analyst David O'Connor initiated coverage: NVDA OW/$300 PT (34% upside), AVGO OW/$460 (26% upside), AMD OW/$600 (15% upside), ARM OW/$320 (21% upside), MRVL OW/$270 (15% upside). INTC initiated Neutral at $110 (4% upside). PTs are modestly below FactSet consensus averages for most names.

bullets.title: NOW: Citi Buy/$154 PT; AI SKU driving 20-30% ACV uplift, FY30 target $30-32B subs
bullets.body: ServiceNow CFO at Citi TMT highlighted 50+ customers spending $1M+ on AI SKUs, driving 20-30% ACV uplift; FY30 subscription revenue target $30-32B with 30% from AI SKUs. Cybersecurity portfolio crossed $1B+ ACV. Upcoming SMB/mid-market AI-native SKU in H2 could dramatically expand TAM. Citi maintains Buy at $154 PT.

bullets.title: LITE: Citi Buy; FY28 guidance raised on OCS TAM >$8B, laser supply tight 2 years
bullets.body: Lumentum management at Citi TMT raised confidence in FY28 guidance (to $40) driven by a larger OCS opportunity — the largest customer requesting more units with TAM potentially exceeding $8B longer-term. Optical bandwidth demand growing 10-40x across DCI/Scale/CPO; laser supply/demand tight for the next two years with favorable pricing. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: STX, WDC: Citi Buy on both; AI storage demand >25% exabyte CAGR, pricing power intact
bullets.body: Citi reaffirmed Buy on both STX and WDC after Citi Tech Conference. WDC management guided >25% exabyte CAGR demand through 2030-31, with price/TB up 18-19% y/y last quarter and further increases expected as drives scale to 44TB+. STX sees AI (inference, agentic, sovereign, video) as structural demand driver beyond traditional HDD cycles; HDDs viable in warm-tier KV cache architectures.

bullets.title: TEAM: Citi TMT takeaways — past peak vibecoding fears; cloud NRR >120%, Rovo gaining
bullets.body: Atlassian management at Citi TMT noted 4Q FY26 revenue $1.8B (+28% y/y); cloud NRR >120%; 80% of F500 use Rovo with assisted actions up 50% q/q. Rovo users show 2x ARR growth vs. non-users; MCP-driven Jira growing 4x. Company cresting heavy R&D cycle, able to reallocate resources. AI cannibalization ('vibecoding') concerns not evident in customer data.

bullets.title: NBIS: Truist initiates Buy/$355 PT (48% upside); Citi Buy/$324 PT on full-stack AI infra
bullets.body: Truist initiated Nebius Group at Buy with $355 PT vs. current $240.35 (48% upside; FactSet avg $297.53). Citi (Buy/$324 PT) highlights Nebius evolving to full-stack AI infrastructure; industry pricing surged to $20-25M/MW for LTAs ($40-50M spot). MSFT and META represent ~40% of FY26 ARR — key concentration risk. Partnership with Palantir for enterprise sovereign AI environments noted.

bullets.title: MRVL: Citi TMT — well-positioned in NPO/CPO; targeting 38-40% OM exit 2026, high-end 2027
bullets.body: Marvell management at Citi TMT indicated NPO/CPO positioning is strong for AI scale-up; expects to exit 2026 near the 38-40% operating margin long-term range and at the high end in 2027. Investor Day on Oct 6 expected to reset long-term targets higher.

bullets.title: VRT down 10% on macro/rates; electricals subsector -2.8%
bullets.body: Vertiv shares fell 10% as the electricals subsector dropped 2.8% amid rising yields (10-yr at 4.84%, highest since Oct 2023), Brent crude topping $100/bbl, and broad industrial weakness. S&P 1500 Industrials fell 1.53% overall.

bullets.title: FOXA -2.1%: DOJ expands probe into Fox-Roku acquisition; Roku -1.6%
bullets.body: DOJ expanded its probe into Fox's $22B Roku acquisition, with concerns focused on potential content favoritism and direct competition between Tubi and the Roku Channel. Fox at GS Communacopia guided record FY27 with Tubi revenue ~35% growth and FOX One targeting 3-5M subscribers over 3-5 years; Roku deal still expected to close H1 2027.

bullets.title: OKLO initiated OW/$55 PT; FSLR initiated OW/$260 PT at Piper Sandler
bullets.body: Piper Sandler initiated OKLO at Overweight with $55 PT, noting its build-own-operate model makes nuclear power bankable for data center demand. FSLR initiated at Overweight/$260 PT as lowest-cost domestic vertically integrated solar supplier. Both initiations came as utilities sector fell 1.2% and solar ETF dropped 2.8% on macro/rates headwinds.

bullets.title: CRM: Salesforce in talks to acquire Listen Labs for ~$2B
bullets.body: Business Insider reported Salesforce has been in discussions to acquire Listen Labs, an AI market research platform, for approximately $2B. The deal has not been finalized.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR +270% y/y in week ending 9/6; 3Q26TD market share 35%
bullets.body: DraftKings surged to 270% GGR growth y/y in New York online sports betting for the week ending 9/6 (hold rate 9.7%, +760 bps y/y), expanding 3QTD GGR market share to 35% vs. 33% prior year. FanDuel remains leader at 38% GGR share. NFL starting one week later in 2026 vs. 2025 created calendar effects.

bullets.title: T: Reaffirms FY guidance ($2.25-$2.35 EPS, FCF $18B+); double-digit EPS growth through 2028
bullets.body: AT&T management at GS Communacopia reaffirmed FY26 guidance (EPS $2.25-$2.35, AEBITDA growth 3-4%, FCF $18B+) and reiterated double-digit EPS growth outlook through 2028. Copper retirement targeting ~$6B in legacy cost removal by end of decade; managing toward 2.5x net debt/EBITDA.

bullets.title: PINS: Cautious GS conference comments on international pressure and European regulatory headwinds
bullets.body: Pinterest declined at the Goldman Sachs conference, citing international business pressure and European regulatory headwinds limiting Asia cross-border sellers. Gen Z ARPU on Pinterest reached parity with Millennials — a positive data point — but regulatory overhang is near-term concern.

bullets.title: ENPH down 5.4%; solar sector weak on macro/rates
bullets.body: Enphase fell 5.4% amid broader solar sector weakness (solar ETF -2.8%) driven by rising Treasury yields (10-yr at 4.84%) and Middle East-driven risk-off. ENPH was attending Jefferies Clean Energy conference with no material new disclosures noted.

bullets.title: HUBS: GS Communacopia — hybrid seat+usage pricing; near-term new-customer adds pressured
bullets.body: HubSpot management noted new-customer additions are under near-term pressure due to longer agent-use-case trials introduced April 2026. AI adoption is uneven, concentrated among early adopters. Monetization model expected as hybrid seats plus usage-based credits tied to outcomes. Users accessing HUBS via OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini show ~12 points better retention than non-users.

bullets.title: DELL: GS Communacopia — AI infrastructure in early multi-year cycle; supply to tighten further in 2027
bullets.body: Dell management framed AI infrastructure demand as early-stage and multi-year, with component availability expected to tighten further in 2027 vs. 2026 (supporting Dell's supply chain advantages). Storage positioned to benefit from AI data growth, and traditional server refresh runway remains from aging installed base and AI agent-driven CPU demand.
